question.text:
Given that

  • $B(x)$ means " $x$ is a bat",
  • $F(x)$ means " $x$ is a fly", and
  • $E(x, y)$ means " $x$ eats $y$ ",

what is the best English translation of

$$
\forall x(F(x) \rightarrow \forall y(E(y, x) \rightarrow B(y))) ?
$$

  1. all flies eat bats
     
  2. only bats eat flies
     
  3. bats eat only flies
     
  4. every bat eats flies
question.subject: Artificial Intelligence

question.text:
Give a compound proposition involving propositions $p, q$ and $r$ that is true when exactly two of $p, q$ and $r$ are true and is false otherwise

  1. $(p \vee q \wedge eg r) \wedge(p \wedge eg q \wedge r) \wedge( eg p \wedge q \wedge r)$
     
  2. $(p \wedge q \wedge eg r) \wedge(p \vee q \wedge eg r) \wedge( eg p \wedge q \wedge r)$
     
  3. $(p \wedge q \wedge eg r) \vee(p \wedge eg q \wedge r) \wedge( eg p \wedge q \wedge r)$
     
  4. $(p \wedge q \wedge eg r) \vee(p \wedge eg q \wedge r) \vee( eg p \wedge q \wedge r)$

question.text:

  1. $\sim Q$
     
  2. $Q$
     
  3. $P \wedge Q$
     
  4. $\sim P \wedge Q$

question.text:
The converse of $((\sim p) \wedge q) \Rightarrow r$ is

  1. $((\sim p) \vee q) \Rightarrow r$
     
  2. $(\sim \mathrm{r}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{p} \wedge \mathrm{q}$
     
  3. $(\mathrm{p} \vee(\sim \mathrm{q})) \Rightarrow(\sim \mathrm{r})$
     
  4. $(\sim r) \Rightarrow((\sim p) \wedge q)$

  1. $(\sim(p \wedge q)) \wedge q$
